summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supply-chain data drops, then build and polish a product that rechecks the launch plan, flags contradictions, and acts through supplier emails and approvals, with a demo and hand-in at 12:00 Sunday.
summary.outcome: Found that the launch plan's 'all ok' hid real shortfalls (art books overbooked by 72,000, failed statues, game cards short). Built and deployed the ask-soony app (polling loop, versioned store, agent, Today/Launch views, sign-off loop, demo instance, README, demo script) on branch jonas/today-flow. Demo rehearsal was still in progress at the end.

repo: Portal data is confidential: keep it in gitignored data/, never put values in code, and never commit .env (only .env.example).

The portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) with no webhooks. Change detection must poll the file list and compare SHA-256, because files are replaced under the same name and formats can change.
New data drops arrive unannounced (five files in the first 37 minutes), so the product needs a fixed poller with a versioned store, with agents working on changed files.
The team workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md: claim work with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md before building.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so a read-only session shows 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.

The demo instance runs on its own hostname via a Cloudflare tunnel and is controlled with scripts/demo.sh (reset, snapshot, stop, CALLS=twilio). It sends supplier emails in dry mode, and the demo DNS record had to be corrected to point at the ask-soony tunnel.
Phone calls are off by default (ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=dry_run in .env) and cost about $0.38 per minute when enabled. The UI polls state every 5 seconds (POLL_MS=5000).

code.finding: New sign-off module: 'Pass it on' sends a one-time /ok/<token> link by push and Teams. Approve runs the chosen option through api.approve once per link and records via=signoff. ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds> auto-approves after a delay as 'simulated', and decline is never simulated.
Lets valid /ok and count-page links bypass the dashboard password; the login page mark was also switched from yellow to ink.
Holds escalate, approve, build_state and the sign-off router. Push goes to every subscribed device, with no per-person targeting.

workflow: Use subagents for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and for parallel builder tasks while the main session writes docs.
Ask before spending money or sending outward-facing messages (calls, supplier emails). Verify what would be sent first.
Verify UI changes in a real browser with a screenshot or scripted keypresses; one claimed fix still needed a second pass.
Keep the repo free of confidential numbers: README has no challenge figures, since the repo goes to the jury.
A mailbox sync that rewrote its stale copy of the action log lost a record. Appending under the shared lock fixed it, and a regression test was added.

friction: The portal token was initially empty in .env, so the API returned 401 and blocked the first data step.
Cloudflare Error 1033 on the demo hostname, because the first DNS route pointed at the wrong tunnel.
J/K navigation skipped or lost the highlight on folded groups of similar cases.
The shared mailbox sync race dropped the 07:58 approval record, though the email did go out.
Browsers cached the old yellow favicon, so a version query parameter and a cache clear were needed.
Routine lines said 'Watching' while switched off, and only the word 'show' was clickable.
Push notifications reach every subscribed device, so the demo needs a second phone to play Maren.
The Boise order confirmation and parts of the data were contradictory or messy (EXW vs DDP, overbooked receipt, a sleeve artwork revision mismatch).
A password was pasted into Discord chat, so it is exposed in history.
open_items: Finish rehearsing the three demo stories end to end on the demo instance; story 3 was still in progress.

Unpushed commits remain (demo script, favicon, J/K, shortcuts, routine fixes). Hand-in work remains: pitch deck, video, final README polish.
